content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository lowRISC_ibex_pr2214, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# Pipeline not being flushed on PMP register clears
In [this commit](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/commit/46404cf86f60f72fb84a2bc693d2ab08011bdb37) the pipeline was made to flush on changes to PMP registers, changes made via `CSR_OP_CLEAR` however are missed.
This is likely because prior to this commit only mstatus and mie were listed, and clearing is safe for those.
This meant that instructions being fetched were passing PMP checks which they should not have been.

1. Select files ONLY FROM THE PROVIDED FILE LIST and specify their FULL PATHS.

```

The root of the problem is in how we detect “PMP‐reg touching” CSRs and then drive the pipeline‐flush signal. In the existing code the flush mask only looks at full‐write operations and never at “clear” ops (CSR_OP_CLEAR), so clearing PMP bits never triggers the flush.

1. rtl/csr.sv – contains the decode of CSR_OP_x and the logic that looks at a PMP‐CSR list to generate a flush.  We need to expand its case on op_type to include CLEAR (not only WRITE or SET).

2. rtl/ibex_core.sv – picks up the flush request from the CSR block and actually squashes the PC/etc.  Make sure it’s wired through for any new CLEAR‐triggered flush.

3. rtl/pmp.sv – holds and updates the PMP registers.  While the CSR block already writes the data, we should double‐check that any CLEAR path (bit‐mask update) is handled the same as a full‐write for state updates.

4. data/csr.svh – the address list of PMP CSRs.  We need to ensure all the PMPADDRx/PMPCFGx CSR addresses are actually in the flush‐mask lookup, and that the CLEAR ops will index into the same lookup.

```  
hw/ip/ibex/rtl/csr.sv  
hw/ip/ibex/rtl/ibex_core.sv  
hw/ip/ibex/rtl/pmp.sv  
hw/ip/ibex/data/csr.svh  
```
